transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-12 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Derek (Apogee Head of Platform), Maya (ML Eng), Samir (CTO)

Summary: quick kickoff to scope POC integration. Jordan opens.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro - Jordan Alvarez, account lead. Priya will lead the tech side. could each of you do a 30s intro?
[00:18] Derek: Derek Lin here, head of platform at Apogee, we own the inference infra for the patient-facing assistants. we're looking to run a short pilot to validate both accuracy and cost profile, um, and see how function calling maps to our backend services.
[00:34] Maya: Maya Ortiz, ML Engineer, i'll be running the benchmarks and the model mapping. our traffic is kinda spiky, peak during hours and then low at night. average seq lengths are around 180 tokens but p95 goes to about 1,200 occasionally.
[00:49] Samir: Samir, CTO. i'm mostly here to understand risk and timeline, security questions mainly.
[00:56] Priya: Great thanks. goal for today: agree success criteria, get workload sizing numbers, and sketch the integration approach (SDK + OpenAI-compat endpoints + function/tool calling + structured outputs). also timeline for a 2-4 week pilot.

--- Topics: success criteria and metrics ---
[01:20] Jordan: quick strawman for success: 1) p95 latency under 600ms for typical sequences (<=256 tokens), 2) output conformity to our JSON schema >98% on automated checks, 3) cost delta vs current baseline under 1.6x. is that in the ballpark?
[01:46] Maya: 600ms p95 sounds tight for our current load but for small seqs it's doable. our current baseline is 420ms p95 on g4-like infra. need to see real numbers across batches.
[02:03] Derek: agree on schema pass rate, we will run a synthetic eval as well as live traffic checks.

--- Workload sizing and logs ---
[02:20] Priya: Maya, can you walk us through the traffic shape, RPS at peak, average tokens per request, and percent of calls that will call tools?
[02:31] Maya: Sure. baseline: 60 RPS peak, 10 RPS median. 65% of requests are short queries (<=128 tokens), 25% mid (128-512), 10% long (>512). tool-calling: about 12% require tool calls to backend APIs (patient lookup, scheduling). small amount will use streaming.
[02:55] Priya: ok that's helpful. for benchmarks we'll create buckets: 1) <=128 tokens, 2) 129-512, 3) 513-1200. also define tool-calling path with KV cache -- sorry, K-V cache -- and external REST calls.

--- Benchmark matrix ---
[03:20] Jordan: matrix should include throughput (RPS), latency p50/p95/p99, token cost, and function-call success rate, plus memory/KV hit rates.
[03:33] Maya: do you recommend running hosted first or go straight to dedicated?
[03:40] Priya: we usually do hosted for speed then dedicated for the final runway. hosted gives quick results for compatibility and correctness; dedicated shows production perf and cost. for p95 targets we'll run hosted baseline then replicate on a 2-GPU reserved pool.
[03:55] Samir: how long does a dedicated pilot take to provision?
[03:59] Jordan: typically 48-72 hours for reserved pool prep. if you need faster we can do temporary burst nodes but costs differ.

--- Integration approach (SDKs & endpoints) ---
[04:15] Priya: On the integration front: we're proposing two parallel tracks: 1) OpenAI-compatible endpoints so your existing SDK/code changes are minimal, and 2) reference SDK snippets (python, node) showing function-calling wiring and streaming. the OpenAI-compat surface will accept the same prompt+functions JSON but we add a few Redwood-specific headers for routing and metadata.
[04:45] Maya: that would be ideal. we already have an OpenAI adapter in prod and want minimal changes. what about structured output enforcement?
[04:54] Priya: we'll show two options: 1) strict schema enforcement server-side with schema validation and automatic retries/fallbacks; 2) lightweight client-side validator in the SDK. for the POC we recommend server-side enforcement + a schema-in-prompt pattern to maximize pass rate.
[05:15] Derek: can you share a sample of the function-calling payload? we need to map it to our scheduling microservice.
[05:22] Priya: yes. i'll share Python and Node snippets. note: function-calling in our OpenAI-compat is compatible with the standard function payload (name, args schema) but we add call-tracing headers. see example in the follow-up.

--- Structured output examples and pitfalls ---
[05:45] Priya: example: output must be a JSON with keys {intent, entities, action: {type, params}}. sometimes models emit text before the JSON or wrap it in triple backticks which breaks downstream parsers; we'll include cleaning heuristics and a multi-pass enforcement step.
[06:05] Maya: we have a pre-processing step that strips non-json prefixes but want the model to reliably emit the JSON. what is typical pass rate?
[06:12] Jordan: across customers we see 85-95% single-pass for instruction-tuned models with schema prompting; with our postvalidate it gets into the high 90s. depends on model family and prompt engineering.

--- Function/tool calling reliability ---
[06:30] Priya: bench will include success rate for function calls, average time to invoke backend (including any K-V cache hits), and error modes. we need to instrument tracing.
[06:42] Derek: are retries automatic? sometimes the function call triggers a side-effect, we need idempotency support.
[06:48] Priya: good call — we'll show idempotency tokens in the SDK and support at the routing layer. we'll also provide a retriable error taxonomy so you can choose safe retries only.

--- Security and compliance ---
[07:05] Samir: SOC2 and SSO are must-haves. also we need KMS integration for keys and audit logs for all function invocations.
[07:16] Jordan: Redwood supports SAML/SSO and has SOC2 docs; we can include KMS integration notes. audit logs are included and we can push logs into your SIEM. will share security questionnaire.
[07:30] Maya: any e2e encryption in transit and at rest?
[07:34] Priya: yes TLS in transit, at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys for Private deployments. for Hosted we offer BYOK via supported KMS providers.

--- Cost discussion ---
[07:50] Jordan: quick note on cost levers: batching, sequence length trimming, quantization, and routing to cheaper variants for non-sensitive workloads. we'll include a cost analysis in the pilot SOW.
[08:03] Maya: we need examples of unit economics per 1k tokens at the sample loads.
[08:08] Jordan: will include both hosted and dedicated estimates in the pricing doc.

--- Timeline & milestones ---
[08:20] Priya: proposed timeline: Week 0: share logs, confirm schema and success criteria. Week 1: run hosted compatibility and baseline. Week 2: dedicated baseline (2GPU pool) + function-calling integration. Week 3: analytics, cost analysis, and final decision. 2-4 weeks total depending on speed of log handoff.
[08:42] Derek: that aligns. i think we can get logs and people assigned this week.

--- Questions and edge cases ---
[09:00] Maya: edge case: long-chat sessions where KV cache grows and memory blowups — how do you manage KV caching across GPU host restart?
[09:12] Priya: we persist KV caches where possible and shard cache entries; runtime supports warm starts and prefix caching heuristics. sometimes recovery leads to degraded perf for a short window, we'll document that.
[09:26] Maya: also curious about streaming partial JSON -- how do you validate when streaming?
[09:32] Priya: we stream tokens but only validate at end; for UX we can provide partial schemas and incremental validation heuristics but final pass ensures correctness.

--- Snippets & integrations ---
[09:50] Priya: snippet (pseudo):
Python example:
response = client.chat.completions.create(model='rwd-compat-1', messages=messages, functions=functions, function_call='auto', headers={'x-rw-trace': '...'} )
if 'function' in response: invoke_local_service(response['function']['name'], response['function']['arguments'])

Node example:
const res = await client.chat.completions.create({ model: 'rwd-compat-1', messages, functions, function_call: 'auto' })
if (res.function) { callService(res.function.name, res.function.arguments) }

[10:35] Derek: that looks close to our adapter, small changes. streaming example?
[10:40] Priya: streaming uses chunked SSE, same protos, we expose a client stream helper in both SDKs.

--- Final recap & next steps ---
[10:55] Jordan: recap: Apogee provides logs and schema; Redwood provides SOW, benchmark matrix, SDK snippets, and security docs. pilot planned to start as soon as logs are in, target first hosted benchmark within one week of handoff.
[11:12] Samir: small ask — include a rollback/fallback plan in case quality regresses during canary.
[11:18] Priya: we'll include automatic fallback to a safe model variant and region routing rules.
[11:25] Derek: ok let's do it.

--- Closing ---
[11:30] Jordan: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with the docs. Priya will share the code samples. talk soon.
[57:30] End of recording (approx)

Notes on transcript quality: Medium - some overlapping speech, occasional mis-transcriptions (K-V vs KV, model names).
